candidate.name: indeterminate
candidate.meaning: A formal symbol that is not a number, the variable of the polynomials U, V and W.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A nonnegative integer less than $2^k$, whose binary representation is padded to length $k$.

judged.note: Use another letter for the indeterminate on radix-digit-convolution (for example X), since z on exact-integer-multiplication is an integer below 2^k.

candidate.name: entry count
candidate.meaning: The number of complex entries in each input and output vector.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of entries in each of the two sequences a and b, and the modulus of the wrap-around.

candidate.name: first vector
candidate.meaning: The first vector of the convolution, of length $q$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The first of the two sequences of length q being convolved, with entries a_0 through a_{q-1}.

candidate.name: second vector
candidate.meaning: The second vector of the convolution, of length $q$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The second of the two sequences of length q being convolved, with entries b_0 through b_{q-1}.

candidate.name: shifted index
candidate.meaning: The index $(l-k)\bmod q$ for fixed $k$, running over $0,\dots,q-1$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an output entry of the cyclic convolution, running from 0 to q-1.

judged.note: Use another letter for the shifted index (l-k) mod q on discrete-fourier-transform (for example r), since t on cyclic-convolution is the output index.

candidate.name: source length
candidate.meaning: The number of entries in each source vector, the length of the source vectors.
candidate.earlier_meaning: A generic binary string whose integer value is taken by the function val.

judged.note: Use another letter for the binary string (for example w), since s on gaussian-resampling is the length of the source vectors.

candidate.name: target length
candidate.meaning: The number of entries in each target vector, the length of the target vectors.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index $(l-k)\bmod q$ for fixed $k$, running over $0,\dots,q-1$.

judged.note: Use another letter for the shifted index (for example r), since t on gaussian-resampling is the length of the target vectors.

candidate.name: target length
candidate.meaning: The number of entries in each target vector, the length of the target vectors.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an output entry of the cyclic convolution, running from 0 to q-1.

judged.note: Use another letter for the output index (for example o), since t on gaussian-resampling is the length of the target vectors.

candidate.name: source vector
candidate.meaning: A length-s vector, the input of the maps S, T and N.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The integer whose i-th digit is u_i.

judged.note: Use another letter for the first integer (for example p), since u on gaussian-resampling is the length-s source vector used by the transform-identity page.

candidate.name: target vector
candidate.meaning: A length-t vector, the input of the maps C and P_t.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.

judged.note: Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on radix-digit-convolution is the digit bit count.

candidate.name: target vector
candidate.meaning: A length-t vector, the input of the maps C and P_t.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The second vector of the convolution, of length $q$.

judged.note: Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on discrete-fourier-transform is the second convolution vector of length q, not a length-t target.

candidate.name: target vector
candidate.meaning: A length-t vector, the input of the maps C and P_t.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The second of the two sequences of length q being convolved, with entries b_0 through b_{q-1}.

judged.note: Use another letter for the target vector on gaussian-resampling, since b on cyclic-convolution is the second sequence of length q.

candidate.name: source entry index
candidate.meaning: The index of an entry of a source vector, which is read modulo s.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of a coefficient of W.

candidate.name: source entry index
candidate.meaning: The index of an entry of a source vector, which is read modulo s.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an output entry, running from $0$ to $q-1$.

candidate.name: target entry index
candidate.meaning: The index of an entry of a target vector.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of bits in a padded binary output, that is, the length to which a binary representation is padded.

judged.note: Use another letter for the padded output length (for example L), since k on gaussian-resampling is a target entry index.

candidate.name: target entry index
candidate.meaning: The index of an entry of a target vector.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an input entry, running from $0$ to $q-1$.

candidate.name: summation index
candidate.meaning: The summation index running over all integers in the expansion of $(Nu)_j$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: An index of the digits of u and v, running from 0 to m-1.

judged.note: Use another letter for the summation index over all integers on gaussian-resampling (for example m'), since i on radix-digit-convolution is a digit index running from 0 to m-1.

candidate.name: last partial-sum index
candidate.meaning: The last index of a partial sum of the Neumann series.
candidate.earlier_meaning: Another linear map, composed with L in the product LM.

judged.note: Use another letter for the last partial-sum index on gaussian-resampling (for example R), since M on operator-norm is a linear map.

candidate.name: first contraction
candidate.meaning: The linear contraction from length-$s$ to length-$t$ vectors, equal to $S'$ on this page.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The map A=S from length-s to length-t vectors in the factored identity.

judged.note: Use another letter for the source map A=S (for example G), since A on transform-identity is the contraction S/2 = S' that operator-norm also uses.

candidate.name: generic length-t vector
candidate.meaning: A generic vector of $t$ coordinates, the input of the permutation $P_t$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The integer whose i-th digit is v_i.

judged.note: Use another letter for the generic length-t vector on transform-identity (for example y), since v on radix-digit-convolution is the second integer.

candidate.name: scaled gathering map
candidate.meaning: The map $S/2$, the gathering map $S$ scaled by one half.
candidate.earlier_meaning: Half of a Gaussian resampling map, used as the map A.

candidate.name: scaled inverse
candidate.meaning: The map $N^{-1}/2$, the inverse of $N$ scaled by one half.
candidate.earlier_meaning: Half the inverse of an invertible map close to the identity.

candidate.name: source index
candidate.meaning: An index of the entries of u, read modulo s.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The power of X whose coefficient in W is taken.

candidate.name: source index
candidate.meaning: An index of the entries of u, read modulo s.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an output entry of the transform, running from 0 to q-1.

judged.note: Use another letter for the source index on gaussian-resampling (the DFT page's j is an output index, the transform's frequency), or say on this page that j here is a position in the source vector u, not the DFT output index.

candidate.name: target index
candidate.meaning: An index of the entries of g, read modulo t.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index of an input entry of the transform, running from 0 to q-1.

candidate.name: Neumann index
candidate.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series $\sum_{r\ge0}E^r$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The index $(l-k) \bmod q$ for fixed $k$, which runs over $0,\dots,q-1$ as $l$ does.

judged.note: Use another letter for the Neumann summation index on gaussian-resampling, since r on the DFT page is the shifted index (l-k) mod q running over 0 to q-1.

candidate.name: precision parameter
candidate.meaning: The integer precision parameter, greater than 100, in the hypotheses of the estimate.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The first of the two integers being multiplied, below 2^{bm}.

judged.note: Use another letter for the precision parameter on gaussian-resampling, since p on the radix-digit convolution page is the first integer being multiplied.
